key_insight: A hybrid silicon nanocone–nanohole architecture boosts thin-film solar absorption by reducing front reflection and trapping longer-wavelength light inside the absorber.
engineering_relevance: The design offers a practical light-management route to raise efficiency and thermal robustness in compact thin-film silicon photovoltaic devices.
method: Front-surface silicon nanocones create a gradual refractive-index transition to suppress reflection.
Embedded air-filled nanoholes increase scattering and internal reflection for stronger optical confinement.
FDTD-based structural optimization is coupled with electrical and opto-electro-thermal device modeling.
evidence_signal: Optimized simulations report 34.64 mA cm-2 Jsc, 0.82 V Voc, 86.27% FF, and 24.42% efficiency, with 95.21% efficiency retained up to 45°C.
watch_item: The reported gains are simulation-based, so fabrication complexity, dimensional tolerances, and real-world defect losses could reduce practical performance.
paper_title: Hybrid Nanocone-Nanohole Light Trapping for High-Efficiency Thin-Film Silicon Solar Cells
